active.title: Swim at Astoria Pool
active.description: One of the largest public outdoor pools in the US — Olympic-size, built in 1936, open all summer in the middle of Queens. Arrive before 10am for a lane.
active.bonus: Swim 20 laps before getting out. No resting at the wall — just turn and keep going.

active.title: Pickup Soccer in Astoria Park
active.description: Queens' biggest park sits on the East River with views of the Hell Gate Bridge — pickup games run on the grass fields most mornings during the Cup. Show up and find one.
active.bonus: Introduce yourself to every player before the game starts. Names before the ball drops.

active.title: Citi Bike the Brooklyn Bridge
active.description: Rent a Citi Bike in Manhattan, ride across the Brooklyn Bridge, continue through DUMBO to the waterfront, and take the ferry back — wheel one way, water the other.
active.bonus: Be on the bridge before 8am. The tourist crowd arrives at 9 — be long gone.

social.title: Rooftop at 230 Fifth
social.description: The most famous rooftop bar in New York — an open-air terrace with an unobstructed view of the Empire State Building. Go at dusk when the lights come on.
social.bonus: Find someone from another country and ask what brought them to New York. Actually listen to the whole answer.

social.title: World Cup Watch Party
social.description: Find a Manhattan bar packed for the match — the atmosphere at a good New York bar during the World Cup is a different kind of alive than anywhere else.
social.bonus: Talk to someone supporting the opposite team. Find out where they came from.

social.title: FIFA Fan Festival
social.description: The official free fan zone in Manhattan — live match screenings, international food, street performers, and a crowd from every country in the world converging on one place.
social.bonus: Find a fan group from a country you know nothing about. Learn one thing about their team before you leave.

chill.title: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
chill.description: 52 acres of curated gardens in the middle of Brooklyn — the Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden is one of the oldest Japanese-inspired gardens in America.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest living thing in the garden. Ask a staff member if you have to. Learn its story.

chill.title: The Met on a Friday Night
chill.description: The Metropolitan Museum stays open until 9pm on Fridays — the crowds thin after 6 and the galleries feel like yours.
chill.bonus: Pick one wing you've never been to and spend your whole visit there. Don't default to the Egyptian wing.

foodie.title: Dinner at Carbone
foodie.description: The most theatrical Italian-American dinner in New York — red sauce classics executed with total commitment in a room that makes you feel like someone important.
foodie.bonus: Order the spicy rigatoni vodka. Non-negotiable. Let the waiter upsell you on one thing.

adventure.title: Midnight Photography Walk
adventure.description: Nikon out, no destination — walk from Midtown south through SoHo to the Financial District after midnight when the city is still alive but the crowds are gone.
adventure.bonus: Shoot only what stops you cold. No tourist landmarks — only moments.
